items.stem: Before executing a function call the model requested, what must the application do with the arguments?

options.text: Validate them against the expected schema and permitted values
options.rationale: Correct: arguments must be validated before any execution, especially for sensitive actions.
Emailing arguments is irrelevant and risky.

options.text: Ignore them and run a default
options.rationale: Ignoring requested arguments breaks the feature.

items.stem: What makes the model more likely to call a tool with correct parameters?

options.text: A clear function description and a precise parameter schema
options.rationale: Correct: clear descriptions and schemas guide correct tool calls.

options.text: A longer system prompt full of adjectives
options.rationale: Verbose adjectives do not clarify the tool's contract.
Model version does not replace a clear tool definition.

options.text: Hiding the parameters from the model
options.rationale: The model cannot fill parameters it was not told about.

items.explanation: Correct: clear descriptions and schemas guide correct tool calls.

items.stem: Which TWO controls make a refund tool safe to expose via function calling? (Select TWO)

options.text: Permission the tool to a maximum refund amount
options.rationale: Correct: bounding the action limits damage from an erroneous call.

options.text: Audit every tool call and its outcome
options.rationale: Correct: auditing provides traceability for sensitive actions.

options.text: Let the model refund any amount with no limit
options.rationale: Unbounded refunds are a serious risk.

items.explanation: Correct: bounding the action limits damage from an erroneous call.
